bull.b: The long-dated 191 MW lease provides substantial contracted revenue visibility beyond Bitcoin mining and supports Riot’s transition toward digital infrastructure. Its targeted high NOI margin could create a more predictable and scalable earnings stream as capacity is delivered in phases.

Strong engineering growth, improving margins, and a sizable data-center-focused backlog indicate capabilities that support both internal deployments and external demand. Increased manufacturing capacity may improve execution, shorten equipment lead times, and reinforce Riot’s infrastructure position.

Low power costs and a relatively efficient direct production cost strengthen Riot’s competitiveness in a resource-intensive mining industry. Better operating economics can help preserve cash generation and network competitiveness when mining conditions become more challenging.

bear.b: Persistent losses and negative operating and free cash flow weaken Riot’s ability to fund expansion internally. Continued cash consumption can increase reliance on financing, asset sales, or favorable operating conditions, while negative returns reduce confidence in near-term capital efficiency.

Riot’s data-center strategy requires substantial capital before the planned capacity is fully delivered and generating rent. Large project financing needs introduce execution and funding dependence, while debt and equity requirements could constrain flexibility if construction or commercialization changes.

Bitcoin mining remains a core revenue source, leaving results exposed to cryptocurrency economics and intensifying network competition. Lower Bitcoin prices or a rising global hash rate can compress revenue and margins even when Riot maintains production and infrastructure scale.
